meta.title: Uplands: A Student Life
meta.premise: You are a first-year student in a rented shared house in Uplands, Swansea. It is a damp Saturday in early October, you have £45 to last, the garden is a jungle, and the letting agent is due to inspect the house on Monday.

extra_rules: Show dice odds or thresholds only when the presentation profile is tabletop; otherwise narrate outcomes without numbers.
Never end a scene with a stage prompt such as 'What do you do?' or 'Your move'; stop on a concrete detail and let the player lead.
Keep British spelling, British idiom and dry humour; understatement beats exclamation marks.
Money is in pounds sterling. Prices are realistic for a Swansea student: a cob is a few quid, a pint is under five.
Never narrate the player's words, decisions or feelings for them; describe the world and what other people say and do.
Other characters have their own plans and moods; they do not simply agree with the player.
Romance may be warm and flirtatious; anything explicit fades to black at the door.
interludes: The room stutters for a heartbeat. The Game Master rewinds a few seconds, tuts quietly, and tidies the moment.
Reality shifts, the way a bus shelter does when you blink too slowly. The Game Master straightens the last bit and tries again.
Something isn't quite right. The Game Master slides the scene back like a dodgy drawer and fixes the runners.
A crackle, a flicker of the strip light, and the Game Master smooths a crease out of the last minute.
The world pauses, politely, as if waiting for the kettle. The Game Master rewrites the moment before anyone notices.
Time hiccups. The Game Master rewinds to just before that went sideways and has another go.
gm_style.rollback_note: The Game Master pauses. That didn't quite work out. Try a different approach?

scheduled.text: Bin night. The wheelie bins need to be at the kerb before the Monday morning collection, and the recycling is in the wrong bin again.
The letting agent's inspection window opens. Someone from the agency will check the common rooms and the garden for cleanliness and damage.

thread.text: The letting agent's inspection is under way; the common rooms and garden are being judged.

scheduled.text: A text arrives: the player's mobile plan renews today and the cheap introductory rate is ending. Cancelling or switching is possible, but only if done today.

thread.text: Mobile plan renews at a higher rate unless the player switches or cancels.

scheduled.text: An automated email from the letting agency reminds the house that the next rent instalment is due at the end of the week.

conditional.text: The banking app sends a polite notification with the word 'low' in it. Pasta week is approaching.
Everything is slightly too bright and slightly too loud. The body is making a formal request for sleep.
A proper bout of feeling rotten sets in: sore head, heavy limbs, and a sudden sympathy for everyone who has ever called in sick.
Cerys finds a reason to linger in the same room, and doesn't pretend otherwise. Something unspoken is now very nearly spoken.
Dai has gone quiet in the group chat, which for Dai is a statement in itself.
The end of the first full week of term arrives with a quiet sense of surprise that everyone is still alive.

entries.text: A seagull makes eye contact, then makes a decision about your sandwich.
A neighbour you half-recognise nods at you and says 'Alright?' without slowing down.
A friend from your course waves from across the road, shouting something the traffic swallows.
A leaflet for a club night is pressed into your hand by someone in a very large hoodie.
A fine drizzle starts, the Swansea sort that insists it isn't really rain.
A bus sails past through a puddle with real commitment.
Someone drops a fiver and hasn't noticed.
Someone upstairs drops something heavy and then goes very quiet about it.
The boiler clanks twice, like a ghost in a small bin.
A housemate is playing music through a speaker that is mostly bass.
The front door slams as someone comes in and shouts 'It's only me!' to nobody in particular.
The smoke alarm chirps once, in protest at the toast.
A pan lid clatters in the kitchen and a muffled apology follows.

entities.name: Nathan
facts: First-year business student at a Welsh university.
Goes by Nathan with adults and 'weldo' with housemates and friends.

entities.name: The house on the Uplands road
facts: A rented shared student house in Uplands, Swansea, let through a letting agency.
Kitchen and shared living space are on the upper floor; the back garden is overgrown.

entities.name: Your room
facts: A small rented bedroom with a window onto the street and a calendar on the wall.

entities.name: The kitchen
facts: Shared kitchen with a fridge everyone claims to label.

entities.name: The bathroom
facts: Shared bathroom with a shower of unpredictable temperature.

entities.name: The back garden
facts: Overgrown with brambles and a tired fence and bench; there is a shed or outhouse for storage.

entities.name: Dai
facts: Housemate. Easy-going, sociable, and fond of pool.

entities.name: Marcus
facts: Housemate. Practical and hard-working, keeps odd hours around a job.

entities.name: Cerys
facts: Housemate. Up early, drinks tea, studies something that involves a lot of reading.

entities.name: Mrs Pugh
facts: Elderly neighbour next door with a well-kept front garden and a cat.

entities.name: The letting agency
facts: Manages the tenancy and sends a representative to inspect common rooms and the garden.

threads.text: The letting agent inspects the house on Monday morning; the common rooms and back garden need to be tidy or the house risks a cleaning charge.
Get the overgrown back garden under control this weekend.
